submitter: bugs_open/381 lane — the three generic structured components the library did not have
rationale:
WHY. bugs_open/381's first half made the planner able to SEE what each component can express (migrations 591-593, council ca400ba6, live). That fix was recorded at the time as NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and this submission is the other half. [MEASURED 2026-08-24] the library's 44 structural components are ALL special-purpose — directories, trackers, calculators, quizzes, spec sheets, one pricing table, two carousels, and site-footer, which is chrome. So a planner told what everything can express STILL had nothing generic to choose. Three concrete consequences, all from the same live build: a page headed 'What your shed needs, month by month' shipped four prose blocks with three incidental month names; a 300-word paragraph beginning 'What we check before a tool earns a recommendation' was a checklist written as prose; and a site whose own classification is a BUYING-GUIDE COMPARISON HUB carried zero <table> elements across all seven served pages. Fleet-wide: 64 of 741 pages have any table at all.

WHAT IS BUILT: checklist (unordered criteria, real <ul>), period-calendar (ordered named periods, real <ol>), comparison-table (options x writer-named criteria, real <table> that stacks into labelled blocks on a phone). Three seeds, one component each, following 247_mechanism_flow_component.sql's shape and its three design rules.

REUSE CHECKED FIRST, AND IT CHANGED THE PLAN. A fourth component — 'steps' — was DROPPED after reading mechanism-flow (247), which already draws an ordered process with decision branches. A checklist is a different shape (unordered, each item independently true, no flow between them) and a calendar is a third (periods do not cause one another, and a reader jumps to the one they are in). The near-neighbours were examined and rejected for stated reasons: features/differentiators are marketing claims about us rendered as cards; faq is question/answer pairs; pricing is pricing tiers on brochure sites; gripper-spec-sheet is one product's specs.

THE CLAIMS RISK IS REAL AND IS NOT CLAIMED AS SOLVED. A comparison table is where a writer most wants to invent prices, ratings and scores, and bugs_open/380 found ungated practice claims on this very site while 29 of 48 live sites have no evidence base at all. 247's rule 1 says the ABSENCE of a slot is the control — but a comparison component with no comparable cells is not a comparison component, so that rule cannot be applied wholesale here. What is done instead: NO price, rating, score, rank or winner field exists anywhere in any of the three schemas (asserted in each verify block by regex over the schema); cells are free text under the writer prompt's existing rule 14; every cell's own llm_guidance repeats the prohibition at the point of writing; and a source_note field makes an unsourced comparison VISIBLE rather than merely disallowed. The header states plainly that a prompt instruction is not an enforcement mechanism and that the real control for figures on an evidence-less site is 380's work, not this schema.

A REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND BY RENDERING, AFTER THE SQL VERIFY BLOCKS PASSED. All three templates initially published the literal string '<no value>' into live markup whenever the writer omitted a per-item key. `missingkey=zero` does NOT protect a map[string]interface{}: the zero value of interface{} is nil, and text/template prints nil as '<no value>'. The option's name promises protection it does not give. Every interpolation is now {{if}}-guarded, and 11 render cases (happy path plus 8 degraded: missing optional columns, a row omitting a declared cell, empty-string labels, absent required fields, absent arrays) all pass — the same three cases FAILED before the fix, which is the mutation-style proof. MEASURED 2026-08-24: 0 live page_components carry '<no value>' today (control: 1,907 carry '<section'), so this was a hazard not to introduce rather than damage to repair.

plan.summary: bugs_open/381 second half: add the three generic structured components the library never had — checklist, period-calendar and comparison-table — so the planner made expressiveness-aware by 591-593 has something generic to actually choose. One seed per component, following 247's shape and design rules. All three dry-run applied and rolled back against the live DB; all three verify blocks mutation-proven to refuse; all three templates rendered through text/template with the chassis's own options across 11 cases including 8 degraded ones.

edits.rationale: The owner's wall-of-text was a checklist written as prose: 1,486 words, 14 paragraphs, no list, centred on a 300-word paragraph beginning 'What we check before a tool earns a recommendation'. Unordered by design — for an ordered process mechanism-flow (247) already exists and a near-duplicate was deliberately not built. NO numeric or score field exists (247 rule 1): a checklist invites '9 out of 10 pass this' and a number-shaped slot is an invitation to fill it. The tick is drawn in CSS and aria-hidden — no emoji, and no <svg>, because text inside an svg is invisible to the claims gate.

edits.rationale: The literal motivating case of the bug: a page headed 'What your shed needs, month by month' delivered four prose blocks and THREE incidental month names. Generic over PERIODS rather than hard-coded to months, so a quarterly roadmap, a four-season guide or a six-week programme reach the same component instead of the estate growing a near-duplicate for each. Renders <ol> because the order is meaning and a screen reader should announce it. Compact rows rather than cards: twelve cards is the wall-of-cards the owner complained about in the same review. ⚠ Explicitly NOT the editorial lane's Phase E timeline, and the boundary is agreed with them: theirs is fact-fed dated events with citations that fail closed without an evidence base; this is authored guidance about a RECURRING cycle with no dates and no citations. The header says that if you are putting a year in a period label you want their component.
edits.sketch:
section_type='period-calendar', content_shape='sequence'
fields: eyebrow?, section_title, intro?, periods[] {label, focus, detail?} min_items 3, footnote?
llm_guidance on periods: "If the page or its heading promises 'month by month', emit ALL TWELVE months, named, in calendar order — a four-season summary does not keep that promise and is the defect this component exists to fix."
verify: expresses list+items; template must contain <ol>; no numeric OR DATE-shaped field (regex includes date|year); exactly one <h2>; no <svg>; guarded interpolation
rendered proof: 12 periods -> li=12 inside ol=1

edits.rationale: Zero tables across seven pages on a buying-guide comparison hub; 64 of 741 fleet pages have any table. NAMED CELLS, NOT A POSITIONAL GRID, and this is a reliability decision: the obvious schema (columns[] plus rows[].cells[]) misaligns silently when an LLM emits four columns and a row of three cells — every subsequent cell shifts and the DB row looks valid. Named cells mean a missing value renders empty IN PLACE. The cost is a four-column maximum, which is also the most a phone can carry. Responsive by stacking with data-label + ::before, because the owner complained about mobile card walls in the same review. Row names are <th scope=row>, not <h3> — a heading inside a table cell breaks the table semantics. This is the component carrying the claims risk; see the rationale above for what is and is not done about it.
edits.sketch:
section_type='comparison-table', content_shape='structured_card', visual_density='high'
fields: eyebrow?, section_title, intro?, option_column_label, column_two_label, column_three_label?, column_four_label?, rows[] {name, note?, cell_two, cell_three?, cell_four?} min_items 2, source_note?
verify: expresses table+items; <th scope="col"> AND <th scope="row"> present; EXACTLY 3 data-label attributes (without them the mobile stack shows a cell with no label); no <h3>; schema declares no price|rating|score|rank|stars|percent|count|number|weight field
rendered proof: 4 rows x 3 columns -> table=1 tr=5 td=12 th=8, balanced

grounded_in: [MEASURED 2026-08-24, live DB] The gap being closed: the 44 structural components enumerated BY NAME are all special-purpose (directories, trackers, calculators, quizzes, spec sheets, one pricing table, two carousels) plus site-footer, which is chrome. No generic checklist, steps, comparison-table or calendar component existed.

[MEASURED 2026-08-24, live DB] garden-tools.uk: zero <table>, zero content lists, zero <strong> across all seven served pages, on a site classified as a buying-guide comparison hub. seasonal-planner promised 'month by month' under its own <h2> and carried three incidental month names.
[MEASURED 2026-08-24, live DB, 30d] Fleet: 741 pages / 29 sites; 64 with any table; 327 (44%) with no list, table or <strong> anywhere in their content.

[VERIFIED 2026-08-24, live DB, transactional dry run] All three seeds applied and all three rollbacks executed inside one BEGIN...ROLLBACK. After insertion component_expresses returns {items,list} for checklist, {items,list} for period-calendar, {items,table} for comparison-table — i.e. each is visible to migration 591's planner listing as the thing it claims to be. Generic structural vocabulary moved from 93 prose-only / 39 list-capable / 15 table-capable to 93 / 42 / 17.

[VERIFIED 2026-08-24, rendered through text/template with Option(missingkey=zero), the same engine as executeGoTemplate in call_agent.go] 11 cases all pass with balanced tags and no leaked template syntax: three happy paths (checklist 4 li in 1 ul; period-calendar TWELVE li in 1 ol; comparison-table table=1 tr=5 td=12 th=8) and eight degraded (two-column table, a row omitting a declared cell, empty-string column labels, minimal checklist, required field absent on each of the three, empty arrays).

[VERIFIED 2026-08-24, and it found a real defect the SQL verify blocks had passed] All three templates initially rendered the literal '<no value>' when a per-item key was absent, because `missingkey=zero` yields nil for a map[string]interface{} and text/template prints nil as '<no value>'. Three of the eleven cases FAILED before the guards were added and PASS after — the same cases, the same harness, which is the mutation-style proof that the fix is what changed the outcome.

[MEASURED 2026-08-24, live DB] The '<no value>' hazard is not live damage: 0 of the estate's page_components contain that string. Control in the same query: 1,907 contain '<section', so the predicate can find things. 49 active section templates use {{range}} and share the exposed shape.

[VERIFIED 2026-08-24, mutation testing] Each seed's per-field interpolation guard proven able to REFUSE: unguarding .cell_three in 606 raises '606 VERIFY: {{.cell_three}} is interpolated with NO {{if .cell_three}} guard anywhere'; unguarding .focus in 605 raises the equivalent. An earlier, more literal version of that assertion FALSELY failed on a correctly element-guarded field — the check was wrong, not the template, and it was rewritten to accept both guard styles. That false positive is recorded in the migration header rather than quietly removed.

[VERIFIED 2026-08-24, code read] The 581 birth gate is satisfied rather than bypassed: trg_cc_refuse_null_section_type refuses any section-level non-forked row with a NULL section_type, because the selector queries WHERE section_type = $1 and such a row is silently unreachable while looking healthy in every listing. All three seeds set section_type explicitly and each verify block asserts it is non-NULL.

[VERIFIED 2026-08-24, code read + live DB] Reuse was checked before building: mechanism-flow (247) already draws an ordered process with decision branches, so a fourth 'steps' component was dropped. features/differentiators/faq/pricing/gripper-spec-sheet were each examined and rejected for a stated reason recorded in the seed headers.
plan.risks:
1. THE CLAIMS RISK ON THE COMPARISON TABLE IS THE REAL ONE AND IS NOT SOLVED. Cells are free text, so a writer CAN type an invented price or rating into one, and on the 29 of 48 sites with no evidence base nothing downstream audits it. What is structural: no price/rating/score/rank field exists to fill. What is not structural: the cell guidance, which is a prompt instruction and therefore not a control (owner ruling). This component makes a pre-existing estate-wide exposure easier to reach; it does not create it, and it does not fix it. The honest dependency is bugs_open/380's work.
2. A writer may pad to fill the structure — twelve thin periods, or a fourth column that says nothing. The guidance says so in words ('if two periods would say the same thing, the subject is not periodised'), which is again not a control. Detectable in the acceptance measure as structure rising with no gain in substance.
3. THESE COMPONENTS ARE UNPROVEN ON A REAL BUILD. Every claim above is about the seed, the schema and the rendered template with synthetic data. No page has been built with any of them, because no build has been authorised. The first real use may expose a schema shape the writer handles badly — most likely candidate: whether an LLM reliably emits twelve well-differentiated periods rather than twelve near-identical ones.
4. Fleet-wide CSS variables cannot be contrast-measured the way 247 measured them for one site. The mitigation is that comprehension never depends on a hairline (--color-border measured 1.66 on a real palette, FAILING the 3.0 non-text threshold), plus theme variables with neutral/translucent fallbacks and no light literals. Residual: an unusual palette could still render these with poor contrast, and the existing contrast/render-audit sweep is what would catch it.
5. Adding three components changes what every planner sees on every site, not just the sites that need them. Mitigated by suitable_page_types and by the fact that a planner that does not need a calendar simply does not pick one — but it is a fleet-wide menu change and is stated as such.
6. The mobile stacking pattern (data-label + ::before) is verified by markup inspection, not in a browser. The rendered proof shows all three data-label attributes present on every row; it does not prove the visual result on a device.
